title: Can AI Read Your Mind?
caption:
Can AI read your mind? 🧠

In 2026, AI turned brain signals into sentences, with no surgery. Riya asks, Arjun explains:
1. How a brain becomes data
2. Mind captioning: describing what you see and remember
3. Brain2Qwerty: decoding what you type
4. What it still CAN'T do
5. Why it matters, and mental privacy

Watch till the quiz ⏸️ and drop your answer below 👇

Next up: How AI agents get hacked 📌

#ai #neuroscience #braincomputerinterface #bci #artificialintelligence #aiexplained #techeducation #aiwithsufi

lines.vo: Arjun, I saw a headline saying AI can now read thoughts. Is that real?
lines.cap: Headlines say AI can READ THOUGHTS. Is that real?

lines.vo: Kind of. AI can now turn brain signals into sentences. But not the way you think. Let me show you.
lines.cap: AI can turn BRAIN SIGNALS into SENTENCES. But not how you think.

lines.vo: Step one. A scanner records your brain activity while you see, remember, or type something.
lines.cap: A SCANNER records your brain while you see, remember, or type.

lines.vo: Step two. A decoder, trained on your own brain, turns those patterns into numbers that stand for meaning.
lines.cap: A DECODER turns patterns into numbers that mean something.

lines.vo: And then a language model turns the numbers into words?
lines.cap: Then a LANGUAGE MODEL turns numbers into words?

lines.vo: Exactly. It keeps trying words until its sentence matches the meaning from your brain.
lines.cap: It keeps trying words until they MATCH your brain.

items.s: while lying in an fMRI scanner
when you just recall the clip

lines.vo: In Japan, researchers at NTT built something called mind captioning. People watched short silent videos inside an fMRI scanner.
lines.cap: NTT built MIND CAPTIONING. People watched silent videos in a scanner.

lines.vo: The AI then wrote a sentence describing the video. Who did what, and where. Straight from their brain activity.
lines.cap: The AI wrote WHO did WHAT, and WHERE. From brain activity.

lines.vo: Wait, and it even worked when they only remembered the video?
lines.cap: It worked when they only REMEMBERED the video?

lines.vo: Yes. Recalling a clip lit up a similar pattern, so the AI could still describe it.
lines.cap: Yes. RECALLING a clip gave a similar pattern.

scenes.label: QUIZ 1
scenes.question: Meta's Brain2Qwerty decodes what you TYPE. Which brain signal does it read?

lines.vo: Okay, quiz time. Meta's Brain2Qwerty decodes what you type. Which signal is it reading?
lines.cap: QUIZ: Brain2Qwerty decodes what you type. Which signal?

lines.vo: Pause the video and guess. A, B, or C.
lines.cap: PAUSE and guess. A, B or C?

lines.vo: It's B. It reads the signals your brain sends to plan each finger movement on the keyboard.
lines.cap: B! It reads your FINGER-MOVEMENT plans.

lines.vo: Older methods without surgery got about eight percent of words right.
lines.cap: Older no-surgery methods: about 8% of words right.

lines.vo: Meta's new version, from June twenty twenty six, gets sixty one percent, using a scanner called MEG.
lines.cap: Brain2Qwerty v2: 61% with an MEG scanner.

lines.vo: And the best volunteer?
lines.cap: And the BEST volunteer?

lines.vo: Seventy eight percent. More than half of their sentences came out with one wrong word or less.
lines.cap: 78%. Half their sentences had ONE mistake or less.

lines.vo: So should I be scared? Can someone read my thoughts on the street?
lines.cap: Should I be SCARED? Can someone read me on the street?

lines.vo: No. Each decoder is trained on one person, for hours. Try it on someone else and it barely beats a random guess.
lines.cap: Each decoder is trained on ONE person. On others it barely works.

lines.vo: It also needs a giant scanner, and you have to sit still and cooperate.
lines.cap: It needs a GIANT SCANNER and your COOPERATION.

lines.vo: And the output is a best guess of the meaning, not a word for word transcript of your thoughts.
lines.cap: The output is a BEST GUESS, not a transcript.

scenes.label: QUIZ 2
scenes.question: Can today's AI read your mind WITHOUT your cooperation?

lines.vo: Second quiz. Can today's AI read your mind without your cooperation?
lines.cap: QUIZ 2: Can AI read you WITHOUT cooperation?

lines.vo: The answer is no. Not today. It needs training on you, a scanner, and you willingly taking part.
lines.cap: NO. It needs training, a scanner, and YOU taking part.

lines.vo: The big win is for people who lost the ability to speak. They could communicate again, without brain surgery.
lines.cap: Big win: a VOICE for people who can't speak. No surgery.

lines.vo: But it also means brain data becomes something companies could collect.
lines.cap: But BRAIN DATA could be collected by companies.

lines.vo: Right. That's why mental privacy is becoming a real debate. Your thoughts might need protection, like your passwords.
lines.cap: That's why MENTAL PRIVACY is now a real debate.

recap: Mind captioning: what you see and recall
Needs YOU: trained per person, big scanner

lines.vo: So, can AI read your mind? It can read some meaning, from a willing person, in a lab. Not your secrets.
lines.cap: Some MEANING, from a WILLING person, in a LAB. Not your secrets.
